examples: The reckless driver sped through a red light and nearly caused an accident.
راننده بی‌پروا از چراغ قرمز با سرعت عبور کرد و تقریباً باعث تصادف شد.
Investing your entire savings in one risky stock would be a reckless decision.
سرمایه‌گذاری تمام پس‌انداز خود در یک سهم پرریسک، تصمیمی بی‌پروا خواهد بود.
His reckless comments during the interview angered several important business partners.
اظهارات بی‌پروای او در طول مصاحبه چند شریک تجاری مهم را عصبانی کرد.
miniContext: Someone who is reckless acts without thinking carefully about the danger or consequences of their actions. A reckless driver ignores speed limits and traffic signals, putting both themselves and others at serious risk. The word can also describe careless financial or verbal behavior, such as reckless spending that leads to debt or reckless remarks that damage a relationship. Being reckless is the opposite of being cautious, favoring excitement or convenience over safety and careful thought.

examples: The engineer came up with an ingenious solution to fix the leak without replacing the entire pipe.
مهندس راه‌حلی خلاقانه و مبتکرانه برای رفع نشتی بدون تعویض کامل لوله پیدا کرد.
Her ingenious idea of using recycled bottles as planters won first prize at the science fair.
ایده خلاقانه او برای استفاده از بطری‌های بازیافتی به‌عنوان گلدان، جایزه اول نمایشگاه علمی را برد.
The escape artist was famous for his ingenious tricks that seemed impossible to explain.
آن شعبده‌باز فراری به‌خاطر ترفندهای مبتکرانه‌اش که غیرقابل توضیح به نظر می‌رسیدند، معروف بود.
miniContext: Something ingenious shows exceptional cleverness and originality, often solving a problem in a way that nobody else had thought of before. Inventors are praised as ingenious when they design a simple device that fixes a complicated problem using unexpected materials. Writers can also craft an ingenious plot twist that surprises readers while still making perfect sense in hindsight. Being ingenious requires more than intelligence alone; it demands creativity and the ability to see solutions others have completely missed.

examples: Buying rice in bulk is far more economical than purchasing small bags every week.
خریدن برنج به‌صورت عمده بسیار اقتصادی‌تر و کم‌هزینه‌تر از خرید کیسه‌های کوچک هر هفته است.
This small car is economical to run because it uses very little fuel.
این ماشین کوچک اقتصادی است چون سوخت بسیار کمی مصرف می‌کند.
She writes in an economical style, using short sentences without a single wasted word.
او با سبکی کم‌واژه و اقتصادی می‌نویسد، با جمله‌های کوتاه و بدون حتی یک کلمه اضافه.
miniContext: Something economical saves money, resources, or time, making the most of what is available without unnecessary waste. An economical appliance uses less electricity, which lowers monthly utility bills over the years. People also describe writing or speech as economical when it communicates clearly using as few words as possible. Choosing the more economical option often requires giving up a little luxury or convenience in exchange for long-term savings.

examples: Everyone who tried the new restaurant seemed to rave about its homemade pasta.
همه کسانی که رستوران جدید را امتحان کرده بودند، با شور زیاد از پاستای خانگی‌اش تعریف می‌کردند.
Critics continue to rave about the director's latest film, calling it a masterpiece.
منتقدان همچنان با هیجان درباره آخرین فیلم کارگردان صحبت می‌کنند و آن را یک اثر شاهکار می‌نامند.
My sister couldn't stop raving about her trip to Japan for weeks after she returned.
خواهرم هفته‌ها بعد از بازگشتش از سفر ژاپن، نتوانست از تعریف‌کردن با شور درباره آن دست بکشد.
miniContext: To rave about something means to talk about it with great enthusiasm and praise, often because the experience exceeded expectations. Food critics rave about a chef's signature dish, and moviegoers rave about a film that moved them emotionally. People sometimes raise an eyebrow at reviews that rave too much, wondering if the praise is exaggerated. Still, when several unrelated people all rave about the same restaurant or book, it's often a reliable sign that it's worth trying.

examples: She gave a quick glance at her watch before hurrying out the door.
او پیش از عجله کردن به سمت در، نگاه کوتاهی به ساعتش انداخت.
At first glance, the painting looked simple, but it revealed more detail the longer you studied it.
در نگاه اول، آن نقاشی ساده به نظر می‌رسید، اما هرچه بیشتر بررسی می‌شد جزئیات بیشتری نشان می‌داد.
One glance at his face was enough to tell that something was seriously wrong.
یک نگاه کوتاه به چهره او کافی بود تا بفهمی چیزی به‌طور جدی اشتباه است.
miniContext: A glance is a brief, quick look at something, often lasting only a second or two. People exchange a glance across a crowded room when they recognize someone, or take a glance at the clock to check how much time is left. The phrase 'at a glance' describes something that can be understood immediately, without needing a closer or longer look. Though brief, a single glance can sometimes reveal more than an entire conversation.

examples: The family created a monthly budget to keep track of their spending on groceries and bills.
آن خانواده یک بودجه ماهانه تعیین کردند تا هزینه‌های خود برای مواد غذایی و قبوض را پیگیری کنند.
The city council approved a new budget for repairing roads and bridges next year.
شورای شهر یک بودجه جدید برای تعمیر جاده‌ها و پل‌ها در سال آینده تصویب کرد.
We had to cut several items from the wedding budget to stay within our limits.
ما مجبور شدیم برای ماندن در محدوده‌مان، چند مورد را از بودجه عروسی حذف کنیم.
miniContext: A budget is a plan that shows how much money is available and how it will be spent over a certain period. Families create a household budget to manage bills, savings, and everyday expenses, while governments pass a national budget to fund schools, hospitals, and infrastructure. Sticking to a budget often requires discipline, especially when unexpected costs appear. Without a clear budget, it's easy to overspend and end up in financial trouble.

examples: The scientist used special tools to manipulate the tiny components under the microscope.
دانشمند از ابزارهای مخصوص برای دستکاری اجزای ریز زیر میکروسکوپ استفاده کرد.
He was accused of trying to manipulate the stock price by spreading false rumors.
او متهم شد که با پخش شایعات دروغ تلاش کرده قیمت سهام را دستکاری کند.
She felt her brother was trying to manipulate her into lending him money again.
او احساس کرد برادرش تلاش می‌کند او را دستکاری کند تا دوباره به او پول قرض بدهد.
miniContext: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, though the word often carries a negative sense when applied to people. A surgeon must manipulate delicate instruments with extreme precision during an operation, while a dishonest salesperson might manipulate customers into buying things they don't actually need. In technology, software lets users manipulate images and data with just a few clicks. Whether describing physical objects or human behavior, manipulate always involves some degree of skillful, deliberate control.

examples: Mechanics regularly lubricate the engine's moving parts to prevent them from wearing out too quickly.
مکانیک‌ها به‌طور منظم قطعات متحرک موتور را روغن‌کاری می‌کنند تا از فرسایش سریع آن‌ها جلوگیری کنند.
You should lubricate the bicycle chain every few weeks to keep it running smoothly.
باید هر چند هفته یک بار زنجیر دوچرخه را روغن‌کاری کنید تا به‌خوبی کار کند.
The squeaky door hinge needed to be lubricated before it would stop making noise.
لولای در که صدا می‌داد باید روغن‌کاری می‌شد تا سرانجام صدا نکند.
miniContext: To lubricate something means to apply oil or grease so that its parts move smoothly and with less friction. Mechanics lubricate engines regularly to reduce wear and prevent overheating, and cyclists lubricate their bike chains to keep pedaling effortless. Without proper lubrication, metal parts can grind against each other and eventually break down. The process of lubricating machinery might seem like a small maintenance step, but skipping it often leads to much bigger and costlier problems later.

examples: The entire town mourned together after the tragedy that claimed the lives of three firefighters.
کل شهر در کنار هم عزاداری کرد پس از فاجعه‌ای که جان سه آتش‌نشان را گرفت.
Shakespeare's most famous tragedy tells the story of a prince seeking revenge for his father's murder.
معروف‌ترین تراژدی شکسپیر داستان شاهزاده‌ای را روایت می‌کند که به‌دنبال انتقام برای قتل پدرش است.
It would be a tragedy to let such a beautiful old building be torn down.
فاجعه خواهد بود اگر اجازه دهیم چنین ساختمان قدیمی و زیبایی تخریب شود.
miniContext: A tragedy is an event that causes great suffering, sadness, or loss, often involving death or irreversible harm. News reports describe natural disasters, fatal accidents, and violent crimes as tragedies because of the devastating impact they have on people's lives. In literature, a tragedy is also a type of play or story where the main character experiences a downfall, often because of their own flaws, as seen in many of Shakespeare's works. Whether real or fictional, a tragedy leaves a lasting emotional impression on everyone it touches.

examples: The soup had a horrid taste because someone accidentally used salt instead of sugar.
آن سوپ طعم وحشتناکی داشت چون کسی به‌اشتباه به‌جای شکر از نمک استفاده کرده بود.
They had to drive through horrid weather conditions, with hail pounding the windshield the whole way.
آن‌ها مجبور شدند در شرایط آب‌وهوایی وحشتناکی رانندگی کنند، با تگرگی که تمام مسیر به شیشه جلو می‌خورد.
He said some horrid things to his sister during the argument that he later regretted.
او در طول دعوا چیزهای وحشتناکی به خواهرش گفت که بعداً از آن‌ها پشیمان شد.
miniContext: Something horrid is extremely unpleasant, nasty, or disturbing, often strong enough to provoke real disgust or shock. A horrid smell can ruin an entire meal, and a horrid memory from childhood can stay with someone for years. The word is also used when describing cruel or unkind behavior, such as saying horrid things in the heat of an argument. Though slightly informal, horrid conveys a stronger reaction than simply calling something bad or unpleasant.

examples: The driver slowed down to let the pedestrian cross safely at the crosswalk.
راننده سرعتش را کم کرد تا عابر پیاده بتواند با امنیت از خط‌کشی عبور کند.
City officials added more traffic lights after several pedestrians were injured near the school.
مقامات شهری پس از آنکه چند عابر پیاده نزدیک مدرسه آسیب دیدند، چراغ‌های راهنمایی بیشتری اضافه کردند.
As a pedestrian, she always made sure to make eye contact with drivers before crossing the street.
به‌عنوان یک عابر پیاده، او همیشه مطمئن می‌شد پیش از عبور از خیابان با رانندگان ارتباط چشمی برقرار کند.
miniContext: A pedestrian is a person who is walking, especially in an area where vehicles are also present, such as a street or crosswalk. Cities design sidewalks, crosswalks, and traffic signals specifically to keep a pedestrian safe from passing cars. Urban planners increasingly try to make downtown areas more pedestrian-friendly, encouraging people to walk instead of drive. Being a careful pedestrian, like looking both ways before crossing, remains one of the simplest ways to avoid accidents.

examples: The nimble gymnast flipped effortlessly across the balance beam without a single wobble.
ژیمناست چابک بدون کوچک‌ترین لرزشی به‌راحتی روی پارالل بالانس چرخید.
Squirrels are remarkably nimble, leaping from branch to branch without ever losing their balance.
سنجاب‌ها به‌طور قابل‌توجهی چابک هستند و بدون از دست دادن تعادل از شاخه‌ای به شاخه دیگر می‌پرند.
Her nimble fingers moved quickly across the piano keys during the difficult solo.
انگشتان چابک او در طول آن سولوی سخت به‌سرعت روی کلیدهای پیانو حرکت می‌کردند.
miniContext: Someone or something nimble moves quickly, lightly, and with great agility, often with impressive coordination. A nimble dancer can change direction instantly without stumbling, and a nimble mind can quickly solve problems or adapt to unexpected changes. The word is often used for both physical movement, like a nimble athlete, and mental quickness, like a nimble thinker who responds cleverly under pressure. Being nimble generally suggests a combination of speed, control, and grace.
